features.name: post_score_below_median
features.definition: Is the post's observed score below the median post score of the corpus?
features.spec: s = pd.to_numeric(df['post_score'], errors='coerce'); med = s.median(); result = (s < med).astype(float).where(s.notna()); null if post_score missing/malformed. Posts equal to the median count as 0 (not below). Median is computed over all rows of the supplied dataset (about 7 in the 2,000-row corpus).

h0: Posts with post_score_below_median = 1 have the same probability of the OP changing their view as posts with post_score_below_median = 0.
h1: Posts with post_score_below_median = 1 have a lower probability of the OP changing their view than posts with post_score_below_median = 0.
note: Median is taken over the supplied corpus (assumed reference). Posts exactly at the median are grouped with the higher-scored group. The timing of the score measurement relative to the outcome is unknown, and the score may have been affected by or reflect the discussion. post_created_utc does not resolve this. The association is descriptive, not causal. The OLS on binary delta is a linear probability model.
